children: Nvidia Corp. (NVDA, Financials), a leading supplier of AI chips and data-center infrastructure, is part of a growing financing structure that could change how investors assess the risks behind the artificial intelligence spending boom.

Technology companies have provided as much as $300 billion in guarantees for AI data centers and chips over the past year, according to the Financial Times. The arrangements can support projects without immediately appearing as conventional debt on the companies' balance sheets.

The guarantees establish minimum future values for computing equipment or data centers owned by special-purpose entities. If those assets later sell or lease for less than the guaranteed amount, the technology company could be responsible for part of the shortfall.

Broadcom has provided about $29 billion in backing for a vehicle that will purchase chips and lease them to Anthropic. Nvidia has agreed to support as much as 25% of certain infrastructure financing packages and provided $105 billion in guarantees tied to an Ohio data center campus for OpenAI.
Meta has also provided a $28 billion guarantee for a data center venture with Blue Owl.
Morgan Stanley estimates seven major cloud and chip companies have accumulated more than $3.1 trillion in off-balance-sheet commitments and other credit support.

So far, analysts generally view the underlying assets as sufficient collateral. But the equation could change if AI demand slows, equipment becomes obsolete faster or data-center capacity exceeds customer needs.
For investors, the next test is whether AI infrastructure spending generates enough cash flow to support the financing structures behind the boom.

title: Big Tech's $300B AI Bet Hides a Risk Investors Can't Ignore
